paper.title: Bandit Multiclass Linear Classification: Efficient Algorithms for the Separable Case

settings.name_in_paper: Online Multiclass Linear Classification with Bandit Feedback, strongly linearly separable with margin gamma
unmapped: Examples (x_t,y_t) are strongly linearly separable with margin gamma: one hyperplane per class separates it from the rest, sum ||w_i||^2 <= 1
Feedback is a single bit indicating whether the predicted label is correct
Performance measured as number of mistakes (realizable setting)
Features in an arbitrary inner product space with ||x_t|| <= R
settings.definition_quote: strongly linearly separable with a margin $\gamma$ if there exist vectors $w_1, w_2, \dots, w_K \in V$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^K \norm{w_i}^2 \le 1$, $\ip{x_t}{w_{y_t}} \ge \gamma/2$, $\ip{x_t}{w_i} \le - \gamma/2$ ...

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit multiclass classification, strongly separable (lower bound)
unmapped: Strong linear separability with margin gamma
Learner may know the margin gamma
settings.definition_quote:
Let $\gamma$ be a positive real number, $R$ be a non-negative real number and
let $K \le (R/\gamma)^2$ be a positive integer. Any (possibly randomized)
algorithm makes at least $((K-1)/2)\left\lfloor (R/\gamma)^2/4 \right\rfloor$
mistakes in expectation on some sequence of labeled examples $(x_1, y_1),
(x_2, y_2), \dots, (x_T, y_T) \in V \times \{1,2,\dots,K\}$ for some inner
product space $(V, \ip{\cdot}{\cdot})$ such that the examples are strongly
linearly separable with margin $\gamma$ and satisfy $\norm{x_1}, \norm{x_2},
\dots, \norm{x_T} \le R$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit multiclass classification with kernel feature map, mapped examples strongly separable
unmapped: Contexts in an arbitrary set X; the examples mapped by the kernel feature map phi are strongly linearly separable with margin gamma; k(x_t,x_t) <= R^2
settings.definition_quote: the mapped examples $(\phi(x_1), y_1)$, $\dots$, $(\phi(x_T), y_T)$ are strongly linearly separable with margin $\gamma$, $k(x_1, x_1), \dots, k(x_T,x_T) \le R^2$

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit multiclass classification, weakly linearly separable examples in the unit ball of R^d
unmapped: Examples weakly linearly separable with margin gamma (multiclass Crammer-Singer separability, sum ||w_i||^2 <= 1)

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit multiclass classification, weakly separable in R^d, margin known (nearest neighbor)
unmapped: Examples weakly linearly separable with margin gamma in R^d with ||x_t|| <= R
The learner knows the margin gamma (used as nearest-neighbour radius)
settings.definition_quote: Suppose $(x_1,y_1), \ldots, (x_T, y_T) \in \R^d \times \{1,2,\dots,K\}$ are labeled examples that are weakly linearly separable with margin $\gamma$ and satisfy $\norm{x_t} \le R$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit binary classification (K=2), strongly separable, adaptive adversary (ignorant-algorithm lower bound)
unmapped: Examples strongly linearly separable with margin gamma in the unit ball of R^d
settings.definition_quote: There exists $T$ and an adversary that sequentially chooses labeled examples $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_T, y_T) \in \R^d\times \{1,2\}$ such that the examples are strongly linearly separable with magin $\gamma$ and $\norm{x_t} \le 1$

algorithms.name: Bandit Algorithm for Strongly Linearly Separable Examples (K copies of Binary Perceptron)

conditions: examples strongly linearly separable with margin gamma

source.label: theorem:strongly-separable-examples-mistake-upper-bound
source.quote: If the examples $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_T, y_T) \in V \times \{1,2,\dots,K\}$ are strongly linearly separable with margin $\gamma$ and $\norm{x_1}, \dots, \norm{x_T} \le R$ then the expected number of mistakes that Algorithm makes is at most $(K-1) \lfloor 4(R/\gamma)^2 \rfloor$.

results.notes: Quantity is expected number of mistakes, equal to regret vs best (perfect) linear classifier under separability. Bound independent of T; per-round time O(dK).

conditions: examples strongly linearly separable with margin gamma
some inner product space (dimension floor((R/gamma)^2/4)+1 in the construction)

source.label: theorem:strongly-separable-examples-mistake-lower-bound
source.quote: Let $\gamma$ be a positive real number, $R$ be a non-negative real number and let $K \le (R/\gamma)^2$ be a positive integer. Any (possibly randomized) algorithm makes at least $((K-1)/2)\left\lfloor (R/\gamma)^2/4 \right\rfloor$ mistakes in expectation on some sequence of labeled examples ... strongly linearly separable with margin $\gamma$ and satisfy $\norm{x_t} \le R$.

results.notes: Expected number of mistakes lower bound.

symbols.gamma_m: margin of strong linear separability in feature space

conditions: mapped examples (phi(x_t), y_t) strongly linearly separable with margin gamma

source.label: theorem:kernelized-upper-bound
source.quote: If $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_T, y_T) \in X \times \{1,2,\dots,K\}$ are labeled examples such that: the mapped examples are strongly linearly separable with margin $\gamma$, $k(x_t, x_t) \le R^2$, then the expected number of mistakes that Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:kernelized} makes is at most $(K-1) \lfloor 4(R/\gamma)^2 \rfloor$.

results.notes: L_feat here denotes R, bound on sqrt(k(x,x)). Compute polynomial assuming kernel evaluable efficiently (per-round cost grows with number of stored updates).

conditions: examples weakly linearly separable with margin gamma
examples lie in the unit ball of R^d

source.label: corollary:weakly-separable-examples-mistake-upper-bound
source.quote: If $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_T, y_T) \in \B(\zero,1) \times \{1,2,\dots,K\}$ is a sequence of weakly separable labeled examples with margin $\gamma > 0$, then the expected number of mistakes made by Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:kernelized} with kernel $k(x,x')$ defined by \eqref{equation:rational-kernel} is at most $\min (2^{\widetilde{O}(K \log^2 (1/\gamma))}, 2^{\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{1/\gamma} \log K)})$.

results.notes: The Õ is inside the exponents in the paper; recorded with O_tilde notation on the whole expression, which does not exactly capture it. Exact margin gamma'=max(gamma_1,gamma_2) given in Theorem 5 and bound is (K-1) floor(8/gamma'^2). Dimension-free.

conditions: examples in R^d weakly linearly separable with margin gamma

source.label: theorem:mistake-bound-for-nearest-neighbor-algorithm
source.quote: Suppose $(x_1,y_1), \ldots, (x_T, y_T) \in \R^d \times \{1,2,\dots,K\}$ are labeled examples that are weakly linearly separable with margin $\gamma$ and satisfy $\norm{x_t} \le R$. Then, the expected number of mistakes made by Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:nearest-neighbor} is at most $(K-1) \left( \frac{2R}{\gamma} + 1\right)^d$.

conditions: algorithm is ignorant (memory state unchanged after mistakes)
examples strongly linearly separable with margin gamma

source.label: theorem:ignorant-lower-bound
source.quote: Let $\gamma \in (0,1)$ and let $d$ be a positive integer. Suppose $\calA$ is an ignorant algorithm ... There exists $T$ and an adversary ... strongly linearly separable with magin $\gamma$ and $\norm{x_t} \le 1$, and the expected number of mistakes made by $\calA$ is at least $\frac{1}{10} \left(\frac{1}{160\gamma}\right)^{\frac{d-2}{4}}$.

results.notes: Lower bound restricted to ignorant algorithms; adversary is adaptive to the algorithm's prediction distribution.
